meta.title: Jabr — learn by doing
meta.description: Understand how things work. Learn maths, physics, engineering and software through simulations, live code and real projects.

home.title: Understand how things work, <mark>by doing</mark>.
home.lead: Jabr teaches every idea with something you can touch: a simulation to steer, code to run, a problem to crack. Then it connects the ideas, so what you learn in one subject carries into the next.

explore.title: Explore
explore.body: Start from a question — how does a rocket reach orbit? — and go as deep as you like.

courses.title: Courses
courses.body: Structured, university-level courses built from interactive lessons and exam-style practice.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: Build something real, like a rocket flight simulator, and learn what it needs along the way.

doing.title: Learning by doing
doing.body: Sliders, live code and step-by-step problems with feedback. Reading is never the whole lesson.

graph.title: One connected map
graph.body: Every concept lives once in a shared graph, so your mastery carries across subjects and gaps are easy to see.

projects.title: Real projects
projects.body: Projects combine several subjects and link every milestone back to the concepts it uses.

home.tryCaption: No sign-up. Change the speed and angle, then launch.

blocks.tryFirst: Try it yourself first, then check.

tangentZoom.description: A graph of f(x) = {fn} around the point x = {x0}. A secant line runs from that point to the right edge of the window. Zooming in shrinks the window; the curve looks straighter and the secant's slope approaches the derivative.
tangentZoom.live: Zoom {zoom} times. Window width h = {h}. Secant slope {slope}.
tangentZoom.straight: At this zoom the curve and the line are almost indistinguishable. That line is the tangent.

projectile.description: A launcher on flat ground firing a ball at {speed} metres per second, {angle} degrees above the horizontal. Target distance: {target}.
projectile.goal: Land the ball on the flag at {target} m.
projectile.hit: Bullseye! It landed at {distance} m, on shot {shots}.
projectile.short: {by} m short. More speed, or a better angle?
projectile.long: {by} m too far. Ease off a little.

dropTest.description: A hammer and a feather held at the same height on {place}, {air}, ready to be dropped together.
dropTest.prompt: Which one hits the ground first? Make a guess, then drop them.
dropTest.slowMotion: On Earth the drop is over in half a second, so this plays in slow motion.
dropTest.resultTie: A tie. With nothing in the way, mass makes no difference.
dropTest.resultApart: The feather lands {gap} s later. Air is the only thing that changed.

euler.description: A graph of the exact solution and the path Euler's method takes in {steps} steps. A dashed line at the right shows the gap between them.
euler.goal: Add steps until the error is {maxError} or less.

secant.description: A graph with two movable points, at {from} and {to}, and the straight line through them.
secant.drag: Drag on the graph, or use the sliders, to move the two points.

generic.goal: Find two points where the slope is at least {min}.

motion.goal: Find the stretch where the average speed is at least {min}.

limit.description: A graph of the function near x = {a}, with a marker {d} to the left of that point and another {d} to the right.
limit.tableCaption: Values of the function at shrinking distances either side of x = {a}
limit.prompt: Close in on x = {a} from both sides. Where are the values heading?
limit.promptContinuity: Close in on x = {a}. Is the function continuous there?

verdict.continuous: From both sides the values close in on {limit}, and that is exactly the value at x = {a}. Nothing surprising happens here.
verdict.hole: From both sides the values close in on {limit}. That is the limit, even though the function has no value at x = {a}.
verdict.moved-point: From both sides the values close in on {limit}. That is the limit. The value at x = {a} is {value}, and the limit does not care.
verdict.jump: From the left the values close in on {left}; from the right, on {right}. Two different answers, so there is no limit here.
verdict.blow-up: The values keep growing without bound. There is no number they settle on, so there is no limit here.
verdict.oscillating: However close you get, the values keep swinging between −1 and 1. They never settle, so there is no limit here.

tests.defined: The function has a value at x = {a}

derivative.description: A graph of f(x) = {fn} with a movable point at x = {x} and the tangent line there.
derivative.slopeDescription: A graph of the tangent's slope against x, {percent} percent traced.
derivative.goal: Sweep the point across the whole curve to draw its derivative. {percent}% traced.

motion.heightDescription: A graph of the height of a ball thrown upward at {speed} metres per second. At {time} seconds it is {height} metres up.
motion.velocityDescription: A graph of the ball's velocity against time: a straight line sloping down. Now {velocity} metres per second.
motion.accelerationDescription: A graph of the ball's acceleration against time: a flat line at {acceleration} metres per second squared.
motion.goal: Stop the clock at the very top of the flight.
motion.goalReached: That's the top. The velocity is zero, but the acceleration is still {acceleration} m/s².
motion.live: Time {time} seconds. Height {height} metres. Velocity {velocity} metres per second.

vectors.description: A grid with two arrows placed tip to tail: the first is {a}, the second is {b}. A third arrow from the start to the end is their sum, {sum}.
vectors.componentsDescription: A grid with one arrow, {a}, and dashed arrows showing its horizontal and vertical parts.
vectors.showParts: Show the horizontal and vertical parts
vectors.goalComponents: Make a vector with a horizontal part of {x} and a vertical part of {y}.
vectors.drag: Drag an arrow's tip, or use the sliders.

boat.goalDirection: Row so that you travel straight across the river.
boat.goalReached: Straight across, at {sum}. You had to aim at {angle} to do it.

vectors.componentsReached: That's it. Its size is {sum}: the two parts and the vector make a right-angled triangle.

braking.sceneDescription: A road seen from the side. A car travelling at {speed} kilometres per hour, and a fallen tree across the road {obstacle} metres ahead.
braking.graphDescription: A graph of the car's speed against time during the stop: flat while the driver reacts, then a straight line down to zero. The area under it is the distance travelled.
braking.prompt: A tree has fallen across the road {obstacle} m ahead. Will you stop in time?
braking.hit: Too fast. The car is still doing {speed} km/h when it reaches the tree.
braking.goal: Find the fastest speed that still stops before the tree.
braking.goalReached: {speed} km/h is the limit. Just 5 km/h more and you would not stop in time.

push.sceneDescription: A {mass} kilogram block on a level surface, about to be pushed to the right with a force of {force} newtons.
push.graphDescription: A graph of the block's speed against time. The shaded band is the time the push lasts.
push.shaded: The shaded band on the graph is the push. Watch what the speed does when it ends.
push.afterIce: After the push ends, nothing acts along the ice, and the block keeps its speed.
push.afterCarpet: After the push ends, friction is the only force along the floor, and it slows the block to a stop.
push.stuck: The push is too weak to beat friction, so the block does not move.
push.goal: Let go of the block at exactly {speed} m/s.
push.goalReached: There it is: {speed} m/s. There is more than one way to do it.

freeBody.description: A diagram of the object with an arrow for each force chosen so far: {forces}.
freeBody.question: Which forces act on it? Tick every one.
freeBody.missing: {count, plural, one {One force is missing.} other {# forces are missing.}}

hint.weight: Gravity pulls on everything that has mass, and it never switches off.
hint.normal: It is resting on a surface. What stops it sinking in?
hint.tension: There is a rope attached, and it is pulled tight.
hint.friction: Is it sliding against something rough?
hint.drag: It is moving fast through the air, and air pushes back.

normal.default: It is not touching a surface, so there is nothing to push back on it.

tension.default: Nothing is tied to it, so nothing can pull on it.

friction.default: It is not sliding against a surface.
friction.book: Friction only appears when something slides, or tries to. Nothing is pushing the book sideways.
friction.sled: The ice is taken to be perfectly slippery here.
friction.ramp: The ramp is taken to be perfectly smooth here.

drag.default: We are ignoring the air here.
drag.book: The book is not moving through the air.
drag.ball: There is no air on the Moon.

motion.default: There is no such force. Moving things do not need a force to keep them moving, only to change how they move.
motion.book: The book is not even moving. And if it were, it would not need a force to keep going.
motion.skydiver: Steady motion needs no force at all: that is Newton's first law. The real forces here balance each other.
motion.ramp: Nothing pushes the block along the slope. It speeds up because its weight and the normal force do not cancel.
motion.rocket: The thrust is the real upward force. There is no extra force of motion on top of it.

book.name: Book
book.description: A book lying still on a table.
book.outcome: The two forces cancel, so the net force is zero and the book stays at rest.

ball.name: Falling ball
ball.description: A ball dropped by an astronaut on the Moon, on its way down.
ball.outcome: Its weight is the only force, so that is the net force. The ball accelerates downwards.

skydiver.name: Skydiver
skydiver.description: A skydiver falling at a steady speed, before opening the parachute.
skydiver.outcome: Drag has grown to match the weight. The net force is zero, so the speed stays the same. This is terminal velocity.

sled.name: Sled
sled.description: A sled being pulled along smooth ice by a level rope. Ignore friction and the air.
sled.outcome: Weight and the normal force cancel. The rope's pull is left over, so the sled accelerates forwards.

ramp.name: Ramp
ramp.description: A block sliding down a smooth ramp tilted at 30°. Ignore friction and the air.
ramp.outcome: The two forces do not cancel. What is left over points down the slope, so that is the way the block accelerates.

rocket.name: Rocket
rocket.description: A rocket just after lift-off, engine firing. It is still slow, so ignore the air.
rocket.outcome: Thrust is bigger than weight. The net force points up, so the rocket accelerates upwards.

orbit.description: The Earth seen from far away, with a cannon {altitude} kilometres above the ground at the top, set to fire sideways at {speed} kilometres per second.
orbit.prompt: The cannon is {altitude} km up, pointing sideways. There is no air. What happens when it fires?
orbit.dropped: With no sideways speed it simply falls, hitting the ground after {minutes} minutes.
orbit.crash: It falls back to Earth {distance} km round the planet, after {minutes} minutes.
orbit.circle: An orbit. It circles {altitude} km up, once every {minutes} minutes, and never comes down.
orbit.ellipse: An orbit, but a stretched one: it swings out to {highest} km and back to {lowest} km, taking {hours} hours a lap.
orbit.escape: Too fast to come back. It escapes the Earth altogether.
orbit.goal: Find a speed that puts the cannonball into orbit.
orbit.goalReached: In orbit. It is still falling the whole time: it just keeps missing the ground.

gameLoop.description: A graph of a bouncing ball's height against time, as a game running at {fps} frames per second computes it: one dot for each frame, above a thin platform.
gameLoop.sweepHint: Not just where the ball ends up
gameLoop.prompt: Each dot will be one frame: the only moments the game knows where the ball is.
gameLoop.bounced: {count, plural, one {One bounce} other {# bounces}} in five seconds, and the ball is still on the platform.
gameLoop.fell: At {time} s the ball was above the platform in one frame and below it in the next. The game never saw them touch.
gameLoop.stride: Furthest the ball moves in one frame
gameLoop.breakGoal: Break the game: make the ball fall through the platform.
gameLoop.breakReached: Broken. The ball moved further in one frame than the platform is thick.
gameLoop.fixGoal: Now fix it without going above 20 frames per second.
gameLoop.fixReached: Fixed. The game now checks the whole path the ball took during the frame.

questions.correctAfterRetry: Correct. Sticking with it paid off.

placeholders.selfCheck: Write your answer here. It stays on your device.

questions.expressionHelp: Write it in terms of {variables}. Use ^ for powers, and 2x or 2*x for multiplication.

problems.offline: You're offline. Reconnect to check your answer; everything else on this page still works.
problems.failed: That didn't go through. Please try again.

feedback.invalid-response: That answer couldn't be read. Please try again.
feedback.select-more: Everything you picked is right, but there is more to select.
feedback.input-too-long: That is too long to be the answer. Simplify it first.
feedback.input-syntax: That doesn't read as maths yet. Check for a missing bracket or operator, and write functions with brackets, like sin(x).
feedback.input-unknown-symbol: There is a letter or symbol in there that doesn't belong. Check the question for what to use.
feedback.input-unknown-function: That uses a function this checker doesn't know. Available: sin, cos, tan, sqrt, exp, ln, abs.
feedback.input-ambiguous-log: Write ln(x) for the natural logarithm, or log10(x) for base ten.
feedback.input-not-allowed: Use only numbers, the variables in the question and + − × ÷ ^.
feedback.input-not-a-number: That doesn't work out to a number.
feedback.sign-error: Right size, wrong sign. Which direction is positive here?
feedback.power-of-ten: The digits look right, but it's out by a power of ten. Check your units.
feedback.radians-mode: This looks like a calculator in radians mode. The angle is in degrees.
feedback.tests-failed: Some checks didn't pass yet. Read their messages and try again.

codelab.empty: Press Run to see what your code does.
codelab.smallScreen: Easier on a bigger screen, but it works here too.
codelab.tabHint: Tab indents; press Esc then Tab to leave the editor.

status.loading-python: Starting Python. The first time takes a few seconds…

notices.timed-out: Stopped after 30 seconds. Is there a loop that never ends?
notices.unavailable: Python couldn't start. If you're offline, connect once so it can download; after that it works offline.

offline.title: You're offline
offline.body: This page hasn't been saved on this device yet. Pages you have already opened still work, and so do their simulations and code labs.

hint.new: Answer a question that uses this concept and it will start to fill in.
hint.learning: You've started. A few more right answers will move this along.
hint.practicing: Getting there. Keep answering without hints to master it.
hint.mastered: You know this. It will come back in review so it stays fresh.

progress.title: Your progress

progress.emptyBody: Answer a question or finish a lesson and your progress will start to fill in. No account needed.
progress.continueResume: Pick up where you left off
progress.allDone: You've finished every lesson that's written so far. More are on the way.
progress.conceptsEmpty: Concepts appear here once you answer questions about them.
progress.recentEmpty: Master a concept or finish a lesson and it will show up here.

data.body: Your progress lives in this browser only. Clearing site data removes it, and it doesn't follow you to other devices. Export a copy to keep it safe or move it.
